Scenario fixture: aria-prohibited-attr (naming attrs must not be used on naming-prohibited roles)

Each target has a stable id of the form apa_case_NN. Scoped to ~13 pure-text-semantic roles (see rule's implementation notes).

A. Valid

01 — PASS: naming-prohibited role with no naming attribute
02 — PASS: naming attribute is empty/whitespace

B. Invalid

03 — FAIL: aria-label on a naming-prohibited role
04 — FAIL: aria-labelledby on a naming-prohibited role
Label
05 — FAIL: both aria-label and aria-labelledby on the same element (two occurrences)
Label
07 — FAIL: aria-label on role="mark" (widened role)
08 — FAIL: aria-label on role="presentation" (widened role — W3C spec §5.2.8.6 "Roles which cannot be named")
09 — FAIL: aria-labelledby on role="none" (widened role — "none" is "presentation"'s documented ARIA 1.2 alias, identical semantics)
Label

C. Not applicable (skipped, not counted)

06 — NEUTRAL: role does not prohibit naming

D. Roleless elements (no explicit or implicit role at all)

10 — FAIL: aria-label on a roleless span with no content fallback (the emoji-mart case)
11 — FAIL: aria-labelledby on a roleless div with no content fallback
Label
12 — NEUTRAL: aria-label on a tag with a real native role (bare <button>, no explicit role) — not this branch's concern
13 — NEUTRAL: roleless tag not in the curated list (<section>, handled elsewhere in this engine)
14 — NEUTRAL: roleless span with aria-label inside a widget-type ancestor role (exempted)
16 — FAIL: aria-label on a span carrying an INVALID role="" token (not a recognized ARIA role), no content fallback — must fall through to this branch instead of being skipped as "has a real role" (identical markup with the role attribute removed entirely already correctly failed as case 10 does)

Case 15 (roleless element whose content already provides a fallback name — reported as cantTell, not fail) is intentionally NOT included in this fixture: this file's overall outcome is fail (several cases above), and a fail outcome only reports its fail-bucket occurrences, so a cantTell-only case here would silently disappear from this file's own occurrence count. See the dedicated inline-HTML test in aria-prohibited-attr.test.js instead.

End of fixture.
